studies.title: Calcium, vitamin D, or combined supplementation for fractures and falls (systematic review and meta-analysis)

criteria.population: 69 trials, 153,902 participants, adults aged 18 or over; participants in most of the trials (87 %) were community dwelling.
criteria.results: Any fracture RR 1.00 (0.95 to 1.06) for vitamin D alone and 0.91 (0.84 to 0.99) with calcium, high certainty; little to no effect on falls.

studies.title: Network meta-analysis of vitamin D, calcium or both for falls

criteria.intervention_exposure: Vitamin D, calcium or both, by dose band.
criteria.results: Falls RR 0.85 (0.74 to 0.95) at 800 to 1,000 IU/day, RR 0.78 for daily administration of 800 to 1,000 IU/day, RR 0.69 with 25(OH)D of 50 nmol/L or less; doses above 1,000 IU/day increased falls compared with 800 to 1,000 IU/day.

studies.title: Vitamin D, calcium, or combined supplementation for the primary prevention of fractures in community-dwelling adults (USPSTF)

criteria.population: Postmenopausal women; men and premenopausal women covered by an I statement.
criteria.intervention_exposure: Vitamin D 400 IU or less plus calcium 1,000 mg or less.
criteria.results: Grade D against low-dose use for primary fracture prevention; insufficient evidence for higher doses; increases kidney stones.

studies.title: Vitamin D, omega-3 and exercise: bone outcomes (DO-HEALTH)

criteria.results: Bone-density paper only; no fracture or falls outcome seen.

saturation: not reached; stopped at call ceiling reserving verification
